# stringer

This example writes the `String` method of an enum, which is the job of
`golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer`. The whole generator is one template,
`stringer.go`.

    go run ./examples/stringer -package axis -type axis x y z v

The real tool reads the constants from the source. This one takes them as
arguments, so that the example stays about the template.

## The template

The template's `main` parses the flags. This function writes the file:

    func writeStringer(pkg, typ string, names []string) {
        //`// Code generated by the qudy stringer example. DO NOT EDIT.
        //`
        //`package ~pkg
        //`
        //`import "fmt"
        //`
        //`func (v# ~typ) String() string {
        //`	switch v# {
        for _, name := range names {
            //`	case ~name:
            //`		return "~name"
        }
        //`	}
        //`	return fmt.Sprintf("~typ(%d)", v#)
        //`}
        //`
        //`func _() {
        //`	// An "invalid array index" error means that a constant's value changed.
        //`	var x# [1]struct{}
        for i, name := range names {
            //`	_ = x#[~name-~i]
        }
        //`}
    }

The same `return` line, written by hand:

    fmt.Printf("\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s(%%d)\", v)\n", typ)

`go generate` compiles the template into `stringer_gen.go`. The emit function
is the default, `fmt.Printf`, so the generator prints to standard output and
needs no type of its own.
